fact: Namibia's Procurement Policy Unit says the government has developed an e-GP Portal through which all public entities are required to upload procurement plans, bid adverts, bidding documents, bid opening reports and award notices.
The Procurement Policy Unit says all public entities are required to upload their procurement documents to the e-GP Portal; an end-to-end platform is planned as phase two.
World Bank procurement expert Devesh Mishra said Namibia's existing e-procurement portal is in use but only by a few public entities (less than 5%).
Mishra gave a figure for use: the existing e-procurement portal is used by less than 5% of public entities.
The Ministry of Finance announced on 13 October 2022 that the E-GP portal is operational, publishing bid advertisements, documents, opening reports and notices of award online.
The Ministry of Finance said all public entities are required by the E-GP guidelines to use the portal for open national and international bidding, sealed quotations and requests for proposals.
